sidequests.title: Chinatown Food Tour
sidequests.description: Eat your way through Boston's Chinatown in one afternoon: dim sum, soup dumplings, then dessert. Every stop is a short walk from the last, and portions are meant for sharing, so come hungry and bring friends.

stops.address: Beach St & Surface Rd, Boston, MA 02111
stops.description: Meet at the gate at the start of Beach Street.
stops.planned_activity: Meet up and take a group photo.
stops.notes: 2 min walk from Chinatown station (Orange Line).

checklist.label: Take a group photo under the gate
Find the four characters written across the top of the gate

stops.description: Big Cantonese dining room for dim sum. Dim sum is served during the day only.
stops.planned_activity: Share a round of dim sum.
stops.notes: About 2 min walk. Arrive before noon on weekends to beat the line.

checklist.label: Order har gow and shumai for the table
Try one dish nobody in your group has had before

stops.description: Casual Taiwanese spot known for soup dumplings.
stops.planned_activity: Split an order of soup dumplings.
stops.notes: About 4 min walk.

checklist.label: Eat a soup dumpling without spilling the soup

stops.description: Modern Asian comfort food and dessert, finishing the tour on something sweet.
stops.notes: About 3 min walk.

checklist.label: Split a cube toast
Vote on the best bite of the day

sidequests.title: Freedom Trail on a Student Budget
sidequests.description: Walk the heart of Boston's Freedom Trail from Boston Common to the North End for about $12: a graveyard full of Revolution-era names, the Old State House, a matcha break, Faneuil Hall and Paul Revere's own house. Every stop is a short walk from the last, and the red line on the sidewalk does the navigating.

stops.description: The Freedom Trail starts at the Visitor Center on Tremont Street, across from Boston Common.
stops.planned_activity: Start at the Visitor Center and find the red line.
stops.notes: Park Street station (Red and Green Lines) is right at the corner of Tremont St.

checklist.label: Find the red line that marks the Freedom Trail
Grab a free trail map at the Visitor Center

stops.description: A 1660 burying ground where Samuel Adams, John Hancock and Paul Revere are buried.
stops.notes: About 3 min walk.

checklist.label: Find the grave of Paul Revere, Samuel Adams or John Hancock
Find the oldest date you can on a headstone

stops.description: The 1713 State House, with the Boston Massacre site marked on the cobblestones outside. Seeing it from the street is free.
stops.planned_activity: See the building and the marker outside.
stops.notes: About 6 min walk.

checklist.label: Stand on the Boston Massacre site marker
Look up at the balcony where the Declaration of Independence was read

stops.description: Community cafe with a matcha menu, a short walk from the State House.
stops.notes: About 2 min walk. Matcha price is an estimate.

checklist.label: Order a matcha
Sip it on the walk to Faneuil Hall

stops.description: The 1742 hall and Quincy Market food hall, free to walk through.
stops.notes: About 4 min walk.

checklist.label: Find the grasshopper weathervane on top of Faneuil Hall
Walk through the Quincy Market food hall

stops.description: Paul Revere's 17th-century home, one of the oldest buildings in downtown Boston.
stops.notes: About 8 min walk. About $5, and college students pay a little less. Check the current price.

checklist.label: Step inside a house from the 1600s

stops.place_name: Old North Church & Paul Revere Mall
stops.description: The church where two lanterns signaled Paul Revere's ride, with his statue on horseback just behind it.
stops.notes: About 5 min walk. The church interior is ticketed; the steeple and the Mall are free to see.

checklist.label: Find the Paul Revere statue on horseback
Look up at the steeple where the two lanterns hung

sidequests.title: Red Line Brain Crawl: MIT to Harvard
sidequests.description: Ride the Red Line from Kendall to Harvard and hit a science museum, a sticky bun, a wall of legal graffiti and a free art museum, then end with a late-night slice. Museum stops are daytime, so start before lunch.

stops.description: MIT's museum of science, technology and art, with robots, holograms and rotating exhibits.
stops.planned_activity: Explore the museum with your college ID.
stops.notes: Kendall/MIT station (Red Line). The student rate is $10 with a college ID; the museum is open daily 10am to 5pm.

checklist.label: Show your college ID for the student rate
See a robot or a hologram exhibit

stops.description: Bakery cafe known for sticky buns and sandwiches.
stops.notes: About 14 min walk. Or ride the Red Line one stop to Central.

checklist.label: Try the sticky bun to share

stops.description: A walkway where graffiti is legal and the murals keep changing.
stops.notes: About 10 min walk.

checklist.label: Photograph your favorite mural
Find a mural you can't believe someone painted

stops.description: Three museums under one glass roof. Admission is free for everyone; open Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 5pm.
stops.planned_activity: Pick one gallery and stay a while.
stops.notes: Ride the Red Line from Central to Harvard (1 stop). Closed Mondays.

checklist.label: Find the glass roof over the courtyard
Pick one painting to spend a full minute with

stops.description: Harvard Square pizza shop since 1966 that stays open late.
stops.notes: About 9 min walk.

checklist.label: Order a Sicilian slice

sidequests.title: East Boston: Skyline, Slices and Planes
sidequests.description: Ride the Blue Line across the harbor for the best view of the Boston skyline, a classic East Boston pizza, and a beach where planes land right overhead. Santarpio's is cash only, so stop at an ATM first.

stops.description: Waterfront park with views of downtown across the harbor.
stops.planned_activity: Walk out on the pier for the skyline.
stops.notes: About 8 min walk from Maverick station (Blue Line).

checklist.label: Walk to the end of the pier for the skyline view
Spot a ship moving through the harbor

stops.description: Old-school East Boston pizza joint known for brick-oven pies and grilled sausage.
stops.notes: Ride the Blue Line from Maverick to Airport (1 stop), then about 6 min on foot. Cash only, with an ATM inside. Price is an estimate; check hours.

checklist.label: Split a pie with the group
Bring cash. It's cash only

stops.description: Harbor-side beach where planes take off and land at Logan.
stops.notes: Ride the Blue Line from Airport to Orient Heights (2 stops), then about 10 min on foot.

checklist.label: Watch a plane land from the beach
Take a photo with a plane overhead

sidequests.title: Jamaica Plain: Arboretum, Pond and Ice Cream
sidequests.description: Take the Orange Line to the end and walk through Harvard's free Arnold Arboretum, around Jamaica Pond, and finish with ice cream on Centre Street. A few miles of easy walking and one cheap treat.

stops.description: Harvard's living tree museum, free every day from sunrise to sunset.
stops.planned_activity: Walk through the collection to the visitor center.
stops.notes: From Forest Hills station (Orange Line), enter at the Forest Hills Gate and walk about 15 min through the grounds to the visitor center. The visitor center is open 10am to 4pm.

checklist.label: Find a tree with an ID tag and look up what it is
Find the Hunnewell Visitor Center

stops.description: Spring-fed pond ringed by a walking path, with a boat house on its shore.
stops.planned_activity: Walk a loop around the pond.
stops.notes: About 16 min walk.

checklist.label: Walk the path around the pond
Spot the boat house

stops.description: Local ice cream shop on Centre Street.
stops.notes: About 7 min walk. Green Street station (Orange Line) is the closest T stop. Price is an estimate.

checklist.label: Try a flavor you have never had

sidequests.title: Broke in Boston: Under $10
sidequests.description: A full afternoon for the price of one coffee and a bagel: a grand free library, the Public Garden, and the Charles River Esplanade, all by Green Line and on foot. Everything but the coffee is free.

stops.description: Local coffee shop on Newbury Street with bagels and a cozy room.
stops.planned_activity: Coffee and a bagel to start.
stops.notes: Hynes Convention Center station (Green Line) is a short walk away. Price is an estimate.

checklist.label: Order a coffee and a bagel for under $8

stops.description: Landmark library in Copley Square with murals, a courtyard and the grand Bates Hall reading room.
stops.notes: About 8 min walk.

checklist.label: Step into the Bates Hall reading room
Find the courtyard

stops.description: Historic garden with a lagoon, a footbridge and the Make Way for Ducklings statues.
stops.notes: About 14 min walk.

checklist.label: Find the Make Way for Ducklings statues
Cross the lagoon footbridge

stops.address: 47 David G Mugar Way, Boston, MA 02108
stops.description: Riverside path along the Charles, centered on the Hatch Shell.
stops.notes: About 8 min walk. Cross Storrow Drive by the footbridge.

checklist.label: Find the Hatch Shell
Walk the river path with the Charles on your side

sidequests.title: Finals Week Midnight Run
sidequests.description: Two North End stops that stay open when everything else has closed: espresso at a classic Italian cafe, then cannoli at a bakery that never closes. The T doesn't run all night, so check the last train home before you go.

stops.description: Old-school Italian cafe on Hanover Street that stays open late.
stops.notes: Haymarket station (Orange and Green Lines). Listed hours run to about midnight, so check before you go.

checklist.label: Order an espresso and a cannoli
Check the last train home

stops.description: Family-run Italian bakery open 24 hours.
stops.notes: About 3 min walk.

checklist.label: Order a cannoli or a calzone
Take a photo of your late-night haul

sidequests.title: Matcha, the Fens and Free Thursday at the Gardner
sidequests.description: Go on a Thursday: start with a matcha near Fenway, walk the Back Bay Fens, and get to the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum by 5pm, when general admission is free until 9. The first Thursday of the month adds live music in the courtyard.

stops.description: Matcha cafe near Fenway Park.
stops.notes: About 11 min walk from Kenmore station (Green Line). Hours vary by listing (one has Thursdays 2pm to 9pm), so check before you go. Price is an estimate.

checklist.label: Order a matcha
Try a matcha dessert

stops.description: Community garden plots in the Back Bay Fens.
stops.notes: About 7 min walk.

checklist.label: Find the garden plots
Walk the Fens path

stops.description: Free formal rose garden inside the Fens, prettiest in early summer.
stops.notes: About 7 min walk. If it's getting dark, take the busier streets and go with friends.

checklist.label: Find the rose garden

stops.description: A Venetian-style palace of art around a flowering courtyard. Free general admission every Thursday, 5 to 9pm; reserve ahead.
stops.notes: About 8 min walk. Reservations are recommended. The first Thursday of each month adds live music, performances and art making.

checklist.label: Reserve a free Thursday night ticket ahead of time
Find the courtyard
Pick your favorite room
